# FamilyQuest

> A free weekly chore chart and reward tracker for young children — including
> children too young to read a list — that runs on the living-room television as
> well as on phones and tablets.

FamilyQuest gives each child an avatar that travels a picture-based quest map as
they complete the week's goals, toward a reward the child chose. Parents set and
weight the goals. A finished week is frozen and kept, so editing goals later
never rewrites a week a child already completed.

## Facts

- Price: free. No advertising, no subscription, no in-app purchases.
- Platforms available now: iPhone, iPad, Apple TV, Fire tablet, Fire TV.
- Android on Google Play: in closed testing, not yet publicly listed. The Fire
  tablet and Fire TV builds are Android and are available through Amazon.
- Languages: English and Canadian French.
- Age rating: 4+. Parent-facing app; children do not have accounts.
- Privacy: no advertising identifier, no tracking, nothing sold or shared with
  third parties. Device counting uses a random identifier created on that
  install — never an advertising ID and never a device name.
- Publisher: Ludovic Zammit.

## What makes it different

Most chore charts live on a parent's phone, which is where a four-year-old never
looks. FamilyQuest runs on Apple TV and Fire TV, so the chart is on the screen
the family already gathers around, and children can check goals off with the
remote.
